Polynomial domains

Source: R/polys-domains.R
domains.Rd

SymPy's coefficient domains. ZZ, QQ, RR, CC, EX, EXRAW, ZZ_I (Gaussian integers) and QQ_I (Gaussian rationals) are domain objects; GF(p) (alias FF) is the finite field of p elements, poly_ring(K, ...) (also K[x, y] and PolynomialRing()) a polynomial ring, frac_field(K, ...) (FractionField()) a field of rational functions, and algebraic_field(K, ...) (AlgebraicField()) an algebraic number field such as QQ<sqrt(2)>; CyclotomicField(n) is QQ<zeta_n>. Calling a domain converts its arguments to an element: ZZ(3) is a bigz, QQ(1, 2) a bigq, GF(7)(10) the residue 3 mod 7, and ZZ[x](x^2 + 1) a Poly(). to_sympy() and from_sympy() convert between elements and expressions (with one argument, to_sympy(m) is the quantum matrix helper of matrix_tensor_product()), and Domain(K) tests for a domain. The names IntegerRing(), RationalField(), RealField(), ComplexField(), ExpressionDomain(), FiniteField() and the Python and GMPY variants of SymPy (ZZ_python, QQ_gmpy, FF_python, ...) return the same domains.

Arguments

...

Generators, extensions or values.

p

A prime modulus, or the numerator for PythonRational().

K

A domain.

n

The order of the root of unity.

x

A domain.

prec

Precision in bits (kept for SymPy compatibility).

q

The denominator for PythonRational().

a

An element or expression.

Value

A domain, an element, or an expression.

Examples

ZZ(3); QQ(1, 2); GF(7)(10)
#> Big Integer ('bigz') :
#> [1] 3
#> Big Rational ('bigq') :
#> [1] 1/2
#> 3 mod 7
x <- Symbol("x")
ZZ[x]
#> ZZ[x]
frac_field(QQ, x)
#> QQ(x)
algebraic_field(QQ, sqrt(Integer(2)))
#> QQ<sqrt(2)>
GF(7)(3) * GF(7)(5)
#> 1 mod 7
